extracted.intended_audience: patent/chemical indexers, information specialists, and patent searchers who assign CPI/Chemical Indexing codes
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and conventions for assigning CPI chemical indexing codes (Parts A–M, N, P, Q and Manual Codes) to patent documents describing catalysts, reactions, products, auxiliaries, conditions, and activities/uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalysts: general coding (1970 onward)
rubrics_metrics.description: From 1970 forward, all catalysts stated to be novel or produced by a novel process have been assigned applicable fragmentation codes from Parts A: through M:.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a catalyst is stated to be novel or produced by a novel process, apply the usual fragmentation codes from Parts A:–M:. (Manual Codes discussed elsewhere.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalysts searchable with Manual Codes (from 1977)
rubrics_metrics.description: From 1977 forward, all catalysts mentioned in Derwent’s Documentation Abstract of a patent are searchable using CPI Section N Manual Codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the CPI Section N Manual Codes for searching catalysts mentioned in documentation abstracts (see Manual Codes discussion, p.26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalyst Q421 subfield (from 1981)
rubrics_metrics.description: From 1981 forward, all catalysts that appear in the claims or examples of patent documents have been assigned to a separate code subfield coded with the code Q421 (“Catalyst”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If catalyst appears in claims/examples, assign Q421. Then: if catalyst claimed novel or produced by novel process also apply fragmentation codes A:–M:; if NOT stated novel and NOT produced by novel process, apply only the limited set of Chemical Codes listed (see next rubric). Code subfields conventions discussed on p.28.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalyst coding when not novel / not produced by novel process
rubrics_metrics.description: If the catalyst is not stated to be novel and is not produced by a novel process, then only a restricted set of Chemical Codes are assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign only: applicable codes from Parts A: and B: (except Sets B7: and B8:); applicable codes from Sets C0:–C5: for inorganic H, C, N, O, S, and halogens if significant; applicable codes from Sets C6:, C7:, and Subset C81:; the Basic Group code from Set M4:; Q421 and M730 (“Known compound used in a reaction”); applicable codes from Set C8: (“Elements absent”) but only if every element in the catalyst is assigned a fragmentation code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalyst exception: alumina/aluminosilicate (zeolites)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alumina or aluminosilicate catalysts (including zeolites) are not coded in Parts A: through M: because they have specific CPI Section N Manual Codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply Parts A:–M: fragmentation codes to alumina/aluminosilicate catalysts; use the specific CPI Section N Manual Codes instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign N2/N3 only when product is structure-coded
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes from Sets N2: (“Bonds broken”) and N3: (“Bonds formed”) are only assigned to reactions whose products are considered significant enough to the patent to be structure-coded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bonds broken/formed are listed in the same code subfield as the structural indexing of the product; do not assign N2/N3 codes if the product is not structure-indexed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Bonds broken
rubrics_metrics.description: Bonds broken are bonds present in a starting material that are changed to yield new bonds in the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT code as broken bonds: bonds broken in auxiliary compounds; bonds broken in the decomposition of the eliminated parts of a molecule; bonds that are temporarily modified but which are present in the final product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Bonds formed
rubrics_metrics.description: Bonds formed are bonds that are present in a product that were not present in the starting materials or auxiliaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All bonds formed in the product are coded, irrespective of the reactants that contributed the bonded atoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding multistage reactions / intermediates
rubrics_metrics.description: The bonds broken and formed in multistage reactions are coded for each reaction step between one isolable structure and the next in the reaction sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are overcoded in one Code Subfield (the product) unless the intermediate(s) is (are) also coded. Fermentations are excluded from this rule unless intermediate stages are specified (e.g. do not code the entire Krebs cycle for sugar→alcohol). Intermediate products are structure-coded in Parts A:–M: only if stated to be novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: When different functional groups react to give single product — overcoding
rubrics_metrics.description: When different functional groups in the same starting material react to give a single product, the two reactions are overcoded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign codes for each reaction occurring within the same starting material even if they converge to one product; see example listing multiple N2/N3 codes for a single product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural convention — tautomer preference
rubrics_metrics.description: The starting materials and products are considered in the form in which they would be indexed in Parts A: through M:; only the preferred tautomeric form is indexed; alternative tautomers are not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index only preferred tautomeric forms (rules for tautomers elsewhere p.106). Do not consider alternative tautomers when selecting N2/N3 codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural convention — ionic bonds ignored
rubrics_metrics.description: Ionic bonds are ignored in both organic and inorganic reactions for N2/N3 indexing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index covalent bond changes only; example: R3N + CH3I → R3-N+CH3I- is indexed for C-halogen broken and C–N formed, but not for N–halogen formed. Reactions involving only ionic bond changes receive no N2/N3 codes (e.g. salt metathesis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural convention — acid/base salts treated as parents
rubrics_metrics.description: Acid addition and base salts of organic bases and acids are treated as the parent base or acid, unless salt formation or decomposition is the only novel feature of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index the parent form (e.g. index N-H form rather than N-K) unless the N-K (salt) bond is a significant feature; do not index N-K broken unless novel/significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural convention — bonds in elemental reactions ignored
rubrics_metrics.description: Bonds broken and formed in elements are ignored in N2/N3 indexing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index only the relevant bond formed (e.g. H2 + I2 → 2HI indexes only 'H-halogen formed').

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-bond conversion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for converting between single/double/triple bonds: single→double/triple — breaking single not indexed but formation of multiple is indexed; double/triple→single — breaking the multiple is indexed but formation of the single is not indexed; double↔triple — both broken and formed are indexed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When no specific multiple-bond code exists, combine single-bond code with generic codes N201/N202 (broken) or N301/N302 (formed). Examples provided in text demonstrate specific code assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use generic multiple-bond codes when specific code missing
rubrics_metrics.description: If no specific code exists for breaking or forming a particular multiple bond, use the code for breaking/ forming the corresponding single bond together with one of the generic codes N201/N202 or N301/N302.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g. C=S bond formation is indexed N352 (C–S formed) and N301 (Double bond formed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Poly codes (N209 / N309)
rubrics_metrics.description: Either N209 ('Poly, bonds broken') or N309 ('Poly, bonds formed') indicates that one of the codes in Sets N2: or N3:, respectively, is applicable more than once to a particular reaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These codes are assigned from point of view of one unit of product. Do NOT assign Poly when reaction results in two molecules of product (bonds formed not indexed Poly). Assign N209 if two molecules of starting material react and a particular N2 code applies more than once. N209/N309 do not indicate that more than one bond in a structure is broken/formed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isotope handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Different isotopes of an element receive the same code as the element itself would receive; when an element is replaced by one of its isotopes, the bond broken is considered the same as the bond formed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index isotope substitutions using the normal elemental bond codes (e.g. C–H broken and C–H formed for H→D replacement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subheadings applicability (historical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes are applicable from 1963 to Subheadings M0–M4 unless otherwise specified. From 1981 codes apply to all subheadings, unless otherwise specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of historical applicability windows when assigning older patents; some subsets were introduced or changed in 1981/Week 27.

rubrics_metrics.name: N0: pre-1981 general chemical reaction descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes in Set N0: were only assigned prior to 1981/Week 26; in 1981/Week 27 more specific codes in Sets N1:–N5: were introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use N000 for processes not more specifically indexed in N01–N06 or N13–N18 (e.g. condensation). N010 covers addition reactions (not oxidation or reduction). N020 covers splits into more than one product including pyrolysis. Note historical differences when indexing pre-1981 documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: N10: Apparatus; physical process indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: The codes in Subset N10: are assigned to apparatuses and physical processes that are not more specifically covered elsewhere in Set N1:.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: N102 (detection, analytical, diagnostic) is usually searched in combination with other codes; galenical formulation apparatuses are indexed in Set R5:, not N10:.

rubrics_metrics.name: N13: Fermentation; culture indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset N13: covers fermentation/culture, cultivation of bacteria/fungi/virus, enzymatic processes, genetic engineering, tissue/cell culture and related items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subset includes attenuation and use of enzymes but not culture resolution. Reactions indexed in Subset N03: are not also indexed N130.

rubrics_metrics.name: N11: Ring expansion/contraction coding criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Either N111 (ring expansion) or N112 (ring contraction) is assigned if: (a) total number of atoms in a ring is changed; (b) at least two ring members from the previous ring remain; and (c) there is no change in overall number of rings in the ring system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: N111/N112 are always used with a 'ring opening' code (N204 or N205) and a 'ring formation by cyclisation' code (N303–N306). Example: production of naphthalene from benzene would NOT be coded N111.

rubrics_metrics.name: N113 / N114: Carbon chain expansion/contraction criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To be indexed N113 or N114, the number of acyclic C atoms in a straight or branched carbon chain must be altered; the carbon chain must be present in both starting material and product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This excludes carbon chain rearrangements where number of carbons does not change and reactions where the chain is newly introduced (e.g. alkylation of aromatic ring is not chain expansion).

rubrics_metrics.name: N14 Irradiation indexing notes
rubrics_metrics.description: N141 = irradiation by light (infrared/UV). N142 = other irradiation (from 1981 electric discharges also indexed N142). Examples of N142 include gamma-rays, X-rays, magnetisation, demagnetisation, sonic and ultrasonic waves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 1981 forward, electric discharges have been indexed N142 in addition to N120 (electrolytic).

rubrics_metrics.name: N16 Purification/extraction/separation notes
rubrics_metrics.description: N160 (purification/extraction/separation) and its subcodes cover extraction from natural materials, isomer/isotope separation, purification by chemical reaction, other separation processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: N160 does not cover steroids; prior to 1981 N161 only covered steroids. Separation of stereoisomers is indexed in Subset N18:, not in N16:.

rubrics_metrics.name: N17 Racemisation / rearrangement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: N171–N173 cover racemisation, rearrangement/isomerisation, conversion of solid form by physical change. N172 covers changes in position of C atoms and/or heteroatoms between two atoms or groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude H-migrations, D/L and cis/trans conversions, and migrations of a group between radicals from different starting materials. Prior to 1981, N172 was only used when starting material and product contained exactly same atoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: N18 Resolution / stereoisomer production rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset N18: covers resolution and production of stereoisomers; includes DL separation by fermentation or other methods, production of stereoisomers via fermentation/biochemical or other methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: N182 and N184 include enzymatic processes. N184 and N185 include stereoselective processes but exclude reactions in which configuration is maintained without racemisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: N2: Bonds broken (generic descriptors and specific subsets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set N2: lists generic descriptors (N200–N209) and many specific codes for bonds broken (N21: C–C etc, N22: C–H/C–X, N23: C–N etc, N24: C–O/C=O, N25: other C bonds, N26: bonds to H/X, N27: other bonds to N, N28: other bonds broken).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use N200 when no bonds broken or stereochemistry only. Use N201/N202 for unspecified multiple bond breaks in combination with single-bond codes. Note special rules (e.g. N203 for exocyclic benzene bond modification) and poly behavior (N209).

rubrics_metrics.name: N3: Bonds formed (generic descriptors and specific subsets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set N3: lists generic descriptors (N301–N309) and many specific codes for bonds formed (N31: C–C etc, N32: C–H/C–X, N35: other bonds to C, N36: bonds to H/X, N33/N37: C–N and bonds to N, N34: C–O/C=O, N38: other bonds formed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use N301/N302 for unspecified multiple bond formation in combination with single-bond codes. N309 indicates a code in Set N3: applicable more than once. Follow notes on when ring-formation codes N303–N306 apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: N4: Auxiliary compound descriptors (including catalysts, media, reagents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset N4: contains auxiliary descriptors such as N411/N412 (oxidising/reducing agent), N421–N426 (type of medium — acid/basic/anhydrous etc), N430 (condensing agent), N441/N442 (heterogeneous/homogeneous catalytic reactions), N450 (inhibitors), N460 (biological auxiliaries), N470 (polymers as auxiliaries), N480 (reactions in absence of oxygen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: N430 covers reagents causing elimination of simple molecules (do not assign to Mg in Grignard). Undefined catalytic reactions are indexed both N441 and N442. N460 covers enzymes, extracts, proteins, polysaccharides, microorganisms; N480 not used when gas reacts with medium (e.g. CO2 neutralisations).

rubrics_metrics.name: N5: Reaction conditions — Temperature and Pressure coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset N5: contains reaction condition codes: N51 for temperature ranges (e.g. T ≤10°C, 10<T≤30°C, etc.), and N52 for pressure ranges (e.g. P<1 atm, 1≤P<2 atm, ... P>1000 atm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate discrete codes for temperature and pressure ranges; N520 includes reactions under vacuum but not vacuum distillation after a reaction; N521 only indexed if pressure is novel feature of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part P & Q: Codes for activities, properties and uses — assignment rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes in Parts P: (Pharmaceutical/Agricultural) and Q: (Other Chemical Descriptors) are used to search for activities, properties, and uses of compounds/compositions and are only assigned when a patent specifically states that a compound/composition has that activity/property/use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT infer activities/properties/uses — only index when specifically stated. Exceptions: Q110 (certain polymer condensants and monomers) is assigned to process patents whether stated or not. When a generic use is disclosed instead of a specific one, index only the generic (e.g. 'pesticide' P340 rather than 'insecticide' P341). When new uses of a known compound are disclosed, index only the new uses. Part P codes are not assigned to inactive intermediates of active products; Part Q codes may be assigned to intermediates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part P / Q search limitations and cross-section notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Because codes in P: and Q: are only assigned when explicitly stated (and because of coding limitations), these codes do not retrieve all references to compounds having a certain activity/property/use and are most useful for verifying stated activities or limiting structure-search hits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For more comprehensive searching of activities/properties/uses (especially general chemicals), consider using Manual Codes (discussed p.26) in combination with Chemical Codes. From 1981 forward, Part Q codes may be assigned to patents classified in B and C, and Part P codes may be assigned to patents in Section E.

rubrics_metrics.name: P0: General activity descriptors (agricultural usage rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: P0 codes (e.g. P001 Human or veterinary activity, P002 Agricultural activity, P003 Contact, P004 Systemic or stomach) are only used for agricultural (Section C - Agdoc) patents in combination with certain other P codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codes in Set P0: are only used for agricultural patents in combination with P200, P210, P220, P241, P242, P330, P331, P340, P341, or P361. Note P003 is not used for human or veterinary activities and thus not used with P001.
